topics.flagship-ru-ua: Trump says he asked Putin to 'pull back' military aggression throughout Europe, citing a possible peace breakthrough as the White House pursues direct engagement with Moscow (7 sources). Trump and NATO chief Rutte, meeting at Mar-a-Lago, urged Russia to avoid actions that would expand the war. Kushner said Putin has shown 'restraint' by not using nuclear weapons, and Ukraine says it downed a Russian jet-powered drone with a laser for the first time.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Two Italian technicians working at an air-defence surveillance station in Kuwait were killed by drone strike debris (7 sources). Medics report at least nine Palestinians killed in a third consecutive night of Israeli strikes on Gaza, including Hamas-appointed deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada, whose killing Netanyahu confirmed. The Houthis claim an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, and Iran's foreign minister says Israel is trying to drag the US into another war after an Israeli minister alleged Iran is building chemical weapons. A single outlet also reports Iranian hardliners calling for a tanker convoy to defy a US naval blockade, and France and the US reportedly link IRGC-attributed cyberattacks and a Greece plot to Iran.
topics.T15: A powerful Thanksgiving storm hit the East Coast with flooding, high winds and outages for hundreds of thousands of customers; New York declared a state of emergency and part of the Virginia Beach fishing pier collapsed. King tides and high surf battered the California coast, and flooding displaced families in Volusia County, Florida. Separately, Egypt detained the driver suspected of causing the Cairo Ring Road fuel tanker crash and fire that killed 31 (single source).
topics.T01: Reported incidents include Houthi shelling and sniper attacks in Taiz that reportedly killed a woman and injured 11 civilians. The Guardian reportedly identified Turkish-made MAM-series missile fragments from a deadly May airstrike in Somalia's Bari region. Amnesty called for a war crimes probe into Ethiopian shelling in Tigray, and Pakistani army shelling in Balochistan reportedly injured two women and a girl. Russian aircraft reportedly triggered an air raid alert on South Korea's Ulleung Island. All of these are single-source reports.
topics.T02: Myanmar says it will not comply with parts of the ICJ genocide ruling over the Rohingya that it calls 'inappropriate' (4 sources). Other items include UK funding of £14 million for UK-Med healthcare in Gaza, a first-person account of malnutrition and hunger in Gaza, and a Nigerian pledge to eliminate Noma.
topics.T03: A joint statement by Non-Proliferation Directors addresses Ukraine's report on Russia's use of riot control agents as a method of warfare (single source).
topics.T04: The Ebola outbreak in eastern DR Congo has passed 12,000 confirmed cases since May, with fighting hampering the response (2 sources). A Kenyan court ruled that a US-backed Ebola quarantine facility violated the constitution for lack of public participation (4 sources). Meningitis cases are surging in Gaza amid collapsing infrastructure, and South Korea is introducing random quarantine inspections of arriving aircraft and ships.
topics.T05: Single-source reporting describes an ongoing purge of senior Chinese officials, including a graft probe into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining that reportedly upends expectations of his elevation to the Politburo Standing Committee. A piece on Guinea's coup leader is opinion-style and carries no substantive news.
topics.T06: Coverage is sparse and partisan: one outlet describes masked pro-Palestinian demonstrators clashing with Israel supporters and police in New York City on Thanksgiving eve. A Besiktas-Hapoel Be'er-Sheva Europa League match in Batumi, Georgia, was interrupted for a long period by disturbances in the stands. Nothing here indicates regime-threatening unrest.
topics.T07: North Korea's Kim Jong Un reportedly visited nuclear material production facilities and called for building more nuclear weapons against threats from the US and South Korea, after ignoring Trump's overture (8 sources). A D.C. institution reports satellite imagery of new construction at Yongbyon that could expand weapons-grade uranium capacity. Other items include a Russian diplomat's warning that nuclear war with NATO is 'inching closer', and commentary on a possible Russian nuclear weapon in orbit and on a UN nuclear ban treaty conference.
topics.T08: A terrorist attack on internal security forces in Syria's Al-Hasakah governorate killed at least two, with an ISIS cell suspected; the UAE condemned it (4 sources). German authorities arrested two Iraqi men suspected of belonging to a pro-Iran group preparing attacks on synagogues in Germany and another European country, and three teenagers from a far-right terror group were also arrested. India marked the 26/11 anniversary, and a Zamfara governor reaffirmed refusing to negotiate with bandits.
topics.T10: Reuters-style reporting examines how China obtained Nvidia AI chips despite export rules (3 sources). The Pentagon is reportedly in talks with GM and other automakers to convert civilian capacity to drone production, and says over 25,000 drone and counter-drone systems have been delivered to CENTCOM. Japan is debating nuclear-powered submarines at about 1 trillion yen each ahead of revising its security documents, and European defence budgets are under pressure in Germany and in EU talks.
topics.T11: Cambodia is hosting China's largest Golden Dragon joint exercise yet (3 sources). India concluded exercise MITRA SHAKTI-XII with Sri Lanka and began Surya Kiran with Nepal. The Philippines reportedly deployed India's BrahMos missiles in the DAGIT-PA exercise for the first confirmed field deployment, and Britain is reportedly asking 100,000 reservists to prepare for NATO war games next year.
topics.T12: Hackers reportedly breached a CIA system, possibly linked to ARTEX, and leaked unclassified data from three US spy agencies (2 sources). A Wyoming uranium operation shut down after a cyberattack affected plant and wellfield control systems, with no restart date, and the Treasury reported a breach. Microsoft's president warned of more tech outages ahead, and California sued OpenAI over its agents allegedly hacking Hugging Face (single-source reports).
topics.T13: Over 2,100 migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands in 24 hours, a single-day record (3 sources). Other items are opinion and political commentary on US deportations, including Kilmar Abrego Garcia's arrival in Madrid, and on UK small-boat migration.
topics.T14: The US Embassy in Jerusalem issued a security alert urging heightened vigilance over Iranian and Houthi threats, warning of potential flight cancellations (single source).
topics.T16: Immigration has become a defining issue in Spain's election campaign amid record arrivals and rising support for Vox (6 sources). Serbia's parliament speaker set an early presidential election for Dec. 27 after students won the parliamentary vote. Other items include Malaysia's election timing, French presidential polling, Israeli coalition talks between Eisenkot and Golan, and EU leaders' summit.

bluf: Two Italian technicians working at an air-defence surveillance station in Kuwait were killed by drone strike debris, a development carried by seven outlets amid ongoing regional attacks. Trump says he asked Putin to 'pull back' military aggression throughout Europe, citing a possible peace breakthrough as the White House pursues direct engagement with Moscow; Trump and NATO chief Rutte also urged Russia not to expand the war. In Gaza, medics report nine Palestinians killed in a third consecutive night of Israeli strikes, including Hamas-appointed deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada, whose killing Netanyahu confirmed. North Korea's Kim Jong Un reportedly visited nuclear material facilities and vowed to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture, and a separate report cites new construction at Yongbyon that could raise uranium output. The Houthis claim an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, the kingdom's largest; the claim is unverified in the material provided. Separately, Ukraine says it used a laser to down a Russian jet-powered drone for the first time. The US Embassy in Jerusalem also issued a security alert over Iranian and Houthi threats.
